children: SpaceX (SPCX, Financials), the aerospace and satellite communications company led by Elon Musk, is rising in premarket trading as its Nasdaq-100 weighting more than doubles in Monday's quarterly rebalance.

The company's index weighting increases to 2.82% from 1.28%, requiring funds that track the Nasdaq-100 to increase their holdings. Estimates cited by TipRanks suggest the adjustment could generate $15.5 billion to $22 billion in passive buying.
The change comes as more SpaceX shares become available following the expiration of post-IPO lockups. SpaceX is now the seventh-largest Nasdaq-100 company by market value, according to the report.

The company also recently received a $946 million NASA contract for three additional International Space Station missions. Meanwhile, Starship's 14th flight is scheduled for Sept. 28 after being delayed from Sept. 22. The mission is expected to attempt orbital flight and deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites.
Wall Street analysts cited by TipRanks have an average price target of $236.80, implying 55% upside from the reference price, although individual targets vary.
For investors, the key question now shifts from index-driven demand to whether SpaceX's next operational milestones can support its valuation. The Sept. 28 Starship launch is the next major catalyst.

title: SpaceX's Bigger Nasdaq-100 Weight Is Triggering a Major Market Shift
